ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in diamond $ABCD$, $\angle BAD=80^\circ$, the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ intersects diagonal $AC$ at point $F$ and $AB$ at point $E$. Connecting $DF$, what is the value of $\angle CDF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BF, \\
$\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAC=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\times 80^\circ=40^\circ$, \\
$BC=CD$, $\angle DCF=\angle BCF$, AD$\parallel$BC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=180^\circ-\angle BAD=100^\circ$, \\
$\because$EF is the perpendicular bisector of AB, \\
$\therefore$AF=BF, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABF=\angle BAC=40^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBF=\angle ABC-\angle ABF=60^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle DCF$ and $\triangle BCF$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{c}DC=BC\\ \angle DCF=\angle BCF\\ CF=CF\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DCF\cong \triangle BCF$ (SAS), \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CDF=\angle CBF= \boxed{60^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rhombus ABCD, A is on the left side, C is on the right side, D is above, B is below; diagonal AC horizontally connects A and C. Point E is on side AB, point F is on diagonal AC, and line EF is the perpendicular bisector of AB; DF is also connected in the figure. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, additionally connect BF. Because ABCD is a rhombus, diagonal AC bisects ∠BAD, therefore ∠BAF=∠BAC=80°/2=40°. Because F is on the perpendicular bisector EF of AB, AF=BF, triangle ABF is an isosceles triangle, hence ∠ABF=∠BAF=40°. Adjacent interior angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so ∠ABC=180°−80°=100°. Therefore ∠CBF=∠ABC−∠ABF=100°−40°=60°. Also because AC also bisects angle C, ∠DCF=∠BCF; and CD=CB, CF is a common side, so △DCF≅△BCF (SAS). Corresponding angles are equal, obtaining ∠CDF=∠CBF=60°.
